verses.1: In the days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goiim,
verses.2: these kings went to war against Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, which is also called Zoar.
verses.3: All these kings gathered together to fight in the Valley of Siddim, which is the area of the Salt Sea.
verses.4: For twelve years they had served Chedorlaomer, but in the thirteenth year they rebelled against him.
verses.5: In the fourteenth year Chedorlaomer and his allied kings came and defeated several peoples — the Rephaim in Ashteroth-karnaim, the Zuzim in Ham, and the Emim in Shaveh-kiriathaim.
verses.6: They also defeated the Horites in the hill country of Seir, all the way to El-paran near the wilderness.
verses.7: Then they turned back and attacked En-mishpat, which is Kadesh, and defeated the Amalekites and the Amorites who were living in Hazazon-tamar.
verses.8: The kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Bela marched out and lined up for battle in the Valley of Siddim
verses.9: against Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goiim, Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar — four kings against five.
verses.10: The Valley of Siddim was full of bitumen pits, and as the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, some of their men fell into the pits while the rest escaped to the hills.
verses.11: The four kings seized everything in Sodom and Gomorrah — all their food and possessions — and left.
verses.12: They also took Lot, Abram's nephew, who was living in Sodom, along with everything he owned.
verses.13: A man who had escaped came and told Abram the Hebrew. Abram was living near the oaks of Mamre the Amorite, who was a brother of Eshcol and Aner. All three of them were Abram's allies.
verses.14: When Abram heard that his nephew had been taken captive, he called out his 318 trained fighting men who had been born in his household, and he went in pursuit all the way to Dan.
verses.15: During the night Abram divided his men and attacked from different sides. He defeated the enemy and chased them all the way to Hobah, north of Damascus.
verses.16: He brought back everything that had been taken. He also rescued his nephew Lot, along with Lot's possessions and all the women and other people.
verses.17: After Abram returned from defeating Chedorlaomer and the kings with him, the king of Sodom came out to meet him in the Valley of Shaveh, which is called the King's Valley.
verses.18: Then Melchizedek, the king of Salem, brought out bread and wine. He was a priest of God Most High.
verses.19: He blessed Abram and said, "May Abram be blessed by God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth.
verses.20: And blessed be God Most High, who helped you defeat your enemies!" Then Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything he had recovered.
verses.21: The king of Sodom said to Abram, "Give me back my people, but keep all the goods for yourself."
verses.22: But Abram said to the king of Sodom, "I have made a promise to the LORD, God Most High, the Creator of heaven and earth,
verses.23: that I will not take so much as a thread or a sandal strap or anything else that belongs to you. I do not want you to be able to say, 'I made Abram rich.'
verses.24: I will take nothing for myself except what my men have already eaten. But let Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre take their share of what belongs to them."

metadata.source: Based on the Authorized King James Version (1769), reinterpreted through the theology of abiding in Christ.
